items.titleOriginal: Another Bubble Warning: Paying More for the Same Stock in Different Places
items.summaryOriginal: Earlier this month, to much fanfare, the chip maker introduced American depositary receipts to add to its longstanding listing in Korea. Its new ADRs are each backed by one-tenth of a Seoul-listed share and can be converted into a Korean share with little effort. No one in his or her right mind would choose to convert, though, because the U.S. stocks trade at a fat premium to the price in Korea, after adjusting for the currency.

items.summaryOriginal: STORY: Hyundai Motor said operating profit fell by 21% in the second-quarter. The South Korean auto giant's $1.98 billion profit for the April-June period missed analyst expectations. It blamed a range of issues, including weaker vehicle sales, production disruption and higher costs. The weaker results showed the growing challenges faced by the auto industry. Carmakers face rising energy and raw material costs as well as supply chain disruptions linked to U.S. tariffs and conflict in the Middle East. But there were green shoots for investors as Hyundai kept its annual guidance unchanged. It said it plans to boost production and launch new models in the second half. Hyundai further said it expects growth to continue in the third and fourth quarter. Although some analysts warned it would be challenging for Hyundai to achieve its full-year operating margin target of 6.3%-7.3%. They blamed that on difficult market conditions. European rival Renault also reported on Thursday a slight drop in sales volumes for the first half. Growing competition in its key European market from new Chinese competitors hit growth at some of its brands.
